tips.title: Airbrushing: Use a Pressure Regulator
tips.text: When airbrushing, use a pressure regulator to adjust the air pressure to match the viscosity of the paint. This ensures a consistent flow rate and prevents paint from being pushed through the brush too quickly, causing uneven coats.

tips.title: Hand Painting: Use a Masking Fluid
tips.text: Apply a masking fluid (such as frisket or Winsor & Newton's Masking Fluid) to areas where you don't want paint to bleed, allowing you to paint delicate details without worrying about overspray.

tips.title: Primer: Use a Thinner Primer for Small Details
tips.text: When painting small details, use a thinner primer (such as Tamiya's Primer or Vallejo's Primer) to ensure a smooth, even coat that won't obscure fine lines or textures.

tips.title: Decals: Use a Decal Set with a Water-Based Adhesive
tips.text: For decals with a water-based adhesive (such as those from Microscale or Vallejo), apply a small amount of water to the decal and let it sit for a few seconds before applying it to the model, allowing the adhesive to flow and adhere properly.

tips.title: Weathering: Use a Thinned-out Wash for Realistic Gradients
tips.text: To create realistic weathering gradients, thin out a wash (such as Tamiya's Panel Line Wash or Vallejo's Wash) with a small amount of water or thinner, and apply it to the model in a smooth, even motion, allowing the wash to flow into the crevices and recesses.
